about: A popular web server that runs websites and sets up their security certificates for you.

prs.title: Each default header is checked on its own
prs.broken: A settings block can add headers only when a response lacks them. If any one of those headers was already set, every default in the block was skipped, and a condition on the block was ignored for them.
prs.changed: Each default header now checks only for itself, and the block's condition applies to it.
prs.matters: Security headers meant as defaults now get sent.

prs.title: Passwords hashed from a pipe match on Windows line endings
prs.broken: Piping a password into the hashing command kept the Windows line-ending character as part of the password, so logins with the real password were refused. Input with no final newline failed outright.
prs.changed: The command now drops a trailing line ending of either kind and accepts input without one.
prs.matters: A password hashed from a script or file works for logging in.

prs.title: Log folders get usable permissions
prs.broken: With one log permission setting and no file mode, the server created missing log folders that even it could not open, then failed to start.
prs.changed: Those folders now get permissions that match the log file's default, so the server can write into them.
prs.matters: The server starts and writes its logs with that setting.

prs.title: Redirects from PHP-style apps now actually redirect
prs.broken: Apps behind the server can answer with just a 'go here instead' address. The server sent that as a normal 'OK' page, so browsers stayed put instead of following the redirect.
prs.changed: The server now sends it as a redirect, as the standard says and other servers already do. An app that sets its own status still wins.
prs.matters: Logins, form submits and other pages that redirect work the way the app meant.

prs.title: Uploads over the size limit are refused, not cut short
prs.broken: With unlimited buffering turned on, the server ignored errors while reading a request. An upload over the size limit was cut off and passed on as if complete, and the user got 'OK' instead of 'too large'.
prs.changed: Read errors now go through the same path as with a buffer limit, so the server reports them instead of hiding them.
prs.matters: Apps never receive a half upload that looks whole, and users are told when a file is too big.

prs.title: Custom error pages now follow the order you wrote them
prs.broken: A site can set different error pages, like one for 'not found' and a general one for other mistakes. The server checked them in reverse order, so the general page showed up where the 'not found' page should have.
prs.changed: The server now keeps the order written in the settings file.
prs.matters: Visitors see the error page the site owner meant for them.

prs.title: A repeated rule line is now an error, not silently ignored
prs.broken: In the server's settings file, a rule could list two custom conditions. The server quietly used only the first one, so the rule matched more requests than intended.
prs.changed: The server now refuses that setup and says how to combine the conditions into one.
prs.matters: The mistake is caught when the settings load, instead of quietly changing which requests a rule applies to.

prs.title: Pages that exist no longer show 'not found'
prs.broken: One form of a setting that says 'try this file, then that one, else show not found' gave every page a 'not found' error, even pages that existed.
prs.changed: Once one rule in a group has matched, the server now skips checking the rest of that group.
prs.matters: Sites using that setting serve their real pages again.

prs.title: Successful requests are no longer retried into an error
prs.broken: The server can pass requests to backend servers and retry on failure. A retry rule that checked only the request also retried replies that had succeeded, until the user got an error page.
prs.changed: Retries based on the reply now happen only when the rule looks at the reply.
prs.matters: Requests that succeed the first time are sent once and reach the user, instead of failing.

prs.title: The server stopped lying about the size of compressed files
prs.broken: When a program asked only for a file's details, not the file itself, the server reported a wrong size (20 bytes) for compressed files.
prs.changed: The server still sends the right details, but no longer makes up that false size.
prs.matters: Tools that check a file's size before downloading, like download managers and caches, now get the truth.

prs.title: Security settings stay on pages that send early hints
prs.broken: Sites add extra instructions to every reply, like 'always use a secure connection'. If the backend first sent a quick early note (an 'early hint'), those instructions vanished from the final reply.
prs.changed: I save the site's own instructions before handling the early note and put them back afterwards.
prs.matters: Security settings a site asks for now reach browsers every time.

prs.title: Page errors no longer send a broken, half-finished reply
prs.broken: When a page the server fills in before sending (a template) had an error, the error reply still claimed the original file's size but had no content, so it looked cut off.
prs.changed: On any template error, the server now drops the file's leftover details before sending the error.
prs.matters: Visitors and tools get a clean error message instead of a broken reply.

prs.title: No more crash when a backend is down and weights are missing
prs.broken: The server can share visitors between backends by weight (how much traffic each gets). With fewer weights than backends and one backend down, it crashed and visitors got empty replies.
prs.changed: Backends without a weight are now treated as getting no traffic, instead of crashing the server.
prs.matters: A small gap in the setup no longer breaks the site when one backend goes down.

prs.title: Traffic now goes to the least busy server when all are busy
prs.broken: One way of sharing traffic should send each request to the less busy of a few backends. Once all of them were busy, it picked at random, even the busiest one.
prs.changed: I fixed the comparison so only the least busy backends stay in the running.
prs.matters: In a test with a slow and a fast backend, the fast one got 70 of 80 requests instead of 41.

prs.title: An impossible IP mask is caught when the config loads
prs.broken: Caddy accepted IP masks in its log filter that cannot exist, and then logged a blank value instead of the client's address.
prs.changed: I made Caddy reject an out-of-range mask when the config is loaded.
prs.matters: A typo in the log settings shows up at startup instead of quietly emptying the client addresses in the logs.

prs.title: The log filter for query strings reads URLs the way the server does
prs.broken: Caddy can hide secret values in the query string of logged URLs. The filter read the URL differently from the server, so anything after a hash sign slipped past it and was written to the log in plain text.
prs.changed: I made the filter read the URL the same way the server does, so the whole query is filtered.
prs.matters: A token sent in a URL with a stray hash sign no longer leaks into the access logs.

prs.title: Page headers end at the right line in templates
prs.broken: A page can start with a header block that ends with three dots. If the page also had a line of three dashes further down, Caddy ended the header there, and the text in between disappeared.
prs.changed: I made it end the header at whichever closing line comes first.
prs.matters: Pages with a divider line in the body keep all their text.
